name: Things I Quit Doing as a Pro
why_it_works: Admitting what you used to do wrong is disarming. It shows growth, signals insider standards, and quietly tells the viewer what other providers may still be doing. Confession beats claims because the viewer cannot argue with your own past.

hook.pattern: Confess a number of habits you dropped after years in the trade.
examples: {{years}} years as a {{profession}}. Three things I quit doing.
I used to do this to every client. Never again.
Three habits I dropped as a {{profession}}, and why you should care.

variables.example: using clipper guards on every fade

variables.name: why_1
variables.example: it leaves a line nobody asked for

variables.name: quit_2

variables.example: the neckline is what people see all week

cta: Get it done the slow, right way: {{offer}}.

craft.notes: Order the quits so the last one costs the pro something (money, time, convenience). A habit you dropped at your own expense is the strongest proof you care about the client. Keep each why to one plain sentence.

do_not: Frame a quit as something competitors still do by name
Confess anything that implies past harm to a patient or client
Pick habits only other pros would understand
compliance: Dental and chiropractic: describe process changes only; no claims of cures, pain elimination or guaranteed results
Healthcare providers: no patient stories or images without written consent; follow your state board's advertising rules
